digest.component_or_area: review-bot service LLM provider configuration and Bedrock inference cutover
propositions: The review-bot service must be configured to use Bedrock inference profiles (opus/sonnet/haiku) for the frontier/standard/trivial model classes respectively, replacing the default direct Anthropic path, to validate that the provider seam functions correctly in production before client deployments.

The Dockerfile.reviewbot image must install the bedrock extra (pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]) so that pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock is available at runtime, otherwise the first Bedrock call fails with LLMConfigError and the LLM-Review gate stops voting on every landing.

A Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm must exist in CloudWatch, dimensioned by ModelId and computed via metric-math on AWS/Bedrock native metrics, to surface provider-specific degradation that the existing voter-error alarm cannot detect (partial failures that still produce votes).

The kill switch (reverting the three class-slot env vars) must be proven to restore voting on the direct Anthropic path with a real vote produced, demonstrating that the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY credential is retained by design and the recovery path is functional.

The per-pass model split (frontier on opus, standard/trivial on sonnet/haiku) must be preserved after cutover and verified through real production votes and usage logs showing zero direct-Anthropic calls and nonzero cache_read_tokens on the Bedrock inference profiles.

A denied-access drill (IAM block on Bedrock) must confirm the gate fails closed with VOTER_ERROR and no approving vote cast, and that re-enabling access restores normal voting, proving the provider outage is contained rather than masked by cross-provider fallback.
